endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: Transparency requirements should be tailored in a way that best suits the needs of the end users.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether assigning AI-assisted denial reviews to licensed specialty physicians without denial incentives changes denial accuracy or patient outcomes, and no supplied study documents the hazard itself. The one endorsing source addresses transparency for end users and does not speak directly to reviewer licensure or financial incentives.

perspectives.view: The evidence base for this recommendation contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The recommendation currently rests on one guidance document whose quoted language concerns tailoring transparency, which offers only indirect support.

The single endorsing source is a principles document that uses "should" language about tailoring transparency to end users. It does not state requirements for reviewer specialty, licensure, or compensation structure. Payers that adopt this recommendation would therefore be relying on the panel's reasoning rather than on a cited standard that addresses conflicted or unqualified reviewers.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare AI-assisted denial reviews conducted by matched-specialty physicians without denial-linked incentives against reviews by other reviewer types, measuring overturn rates on appeal, time to care, and patient harm. Studies documenting how often AI denials are upheld without substantive reviewer engagement would also establish the size of the hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. Payers cannot tell from this record whether the safeguard would work equally well for groups who may be less able to file appeals after a denial.
